scenario: An operator's incident-management system only logs turbine downtime events exceeding 36 hours. Among logged events the mean downtime is 55 hours (σ=12 h). Engineers need the true mean downtime across all turbine stoppages.

data.description: Observed statistics among units exceeding reporting threshold

values.n_observed: only values above threshold are recorded

question: (a) Assuming the true distribution of downtime duration is normal with σ=12 hours, solve for the true population mean μ such that E[X|X>36]=55. (b) What fraction of all events lie above the above 36-hour alert threshold threshold? (c) By how much does the observed mean overstate the true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: Solving the truncated-normal equation μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 55 numerically gives μ≈53.12758. Only 92.3% of all events are actually observed; the observed mean overstates the true mean by ≈1.8724 hours.

naive_answer: The true mean downtime duration is approximately 55 hours because that is what the data directly show.
naive_trap: The observed mean is a truncated-normal conditional expectation, not the population mean; it always exceeds the true mean for above-threshold samples.
reasoning_trace: (1) Let α=(t−μ)/σ. (2) E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 55 and solve numerically for μ using brentq. (4) Solution: μ≈53.12758. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((36−53.12758)/σ)≈0.92325.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 55,12,36
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-53.12758)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.92325)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
